title: Synthetic air handler: dirty filter and hunting valve (generated by CAMBER)
summary: SYNTHETIC, generated locally by CAMBER (no download, no real building): one constant-volume air handler's outdoor temperature, supply fan status, supply-air temperature, cooling valve and filter differential pressure, every 5 minutes for two weeks of early summer on a daily 05:00-21:00 schedule, as five units: a healthy unit, a filter that loads up and crosses its change-out pressure part-way, a filter far past it, a cooling valve whose PI loop hunts, and one that oscillates a little.
teaches: a dirty filter and a hunting control loop, which no open dataset shows
why a run's median filter pressure can pass a filter that is due for a change
why a hunting loop needs a trend sampled every few minutes: at 10 or 15 minutes it cannot be seen, and the rule says so rather than pass it
publisher: CAMBER (generated locally by the user's copy)
citation: CAMBER synthetic dataset synthetic-ahu-maintenance, generator ahu_maintenance (camber.datasets._synthetic_ahu_maintenance), seed 146. Generated data, not measurements from any building.
timezone: naive generated clock (no DST); 5-minute samples from 2025-06-02 (a Monday) for 14 days
equipment: 1 constant-volume air handler as 5 scenario units

fault_types.dirty_filter: a filter at or past its change-out pressure: one far past it all fortnight, one that loads up and crosses 1.0 in. w.c. part-way
fault_types.hunting: a cooling-valve PI loop tuned too hot: a limit cycle of about 11 minutes, about 20 % of stroke, whenever the unit runs

full.description: all five units (the same as default)

known_issues: Synthetic: generated by CAMBER's own model of an air handler, not measured. It shows what the rules see, not how a real unit behaves; never cite it as evidence about real buildings.
5-minute samples: the hunting loop's 11-minute cycle is resolved at 5 minutes, averaged away when resampled to 10 minutes and aliased at 15 minutes. Keep resample at 5min.

The unit runs 16 hours a day; with the fan off the filter transmitter reads about zero and the valve is shut, and both rules read every sample of the run, so those hours pull the filter median down and the reversal rate with it.
